about: Curated per-building overrides for tools/build-data.mjs (keyed by source OSM id). Heights are metres from the lowest terrain point under the footprint to the roof top (placement.js convention). Entries with "bulk" come from a typology rule (unnamed neighbourhood houses/garages), all others were researched individually — see "notes". Palette/facade objects are shared on purpose so the generic builder can batch materials.

buildings.notes: Hornbostel 1906-12 (Machinery Hall). ~4 storeys + rotunda above the Mall end (~40 m), ~6-7 storeys toward Junction Hollow. Roof ~58.
Hornbostel 1905. 3 storeys on the Mall, extra lower floors stepping down to the Hollow; Baker/Porter share one cornice line (~64.5).
Hornbostel 1914-19; 3 storeys + basement; Baker/Porter 257k GSF over ~8.4k m2 footprint (FMS listing).
Hornbostel 1908, expanded/renovated 2003-05. ~3-4 storeys above the Mall (~51); A/B levels drop to the Gates ravine (~30) so the north face is ~7 storeys. Flat roof with CMU green-roof section.
College of Fine Arts, Hornbostel 1912-16. 3 tall storeys + basement (125k GSF / 3.1k m2).

buildings.nameZh: 玛格丽特·莫里森·卡内基楼
buildings.notes: Hornbostel 1906-14, restored 1990s (Bohlin Cywinski Jackson). ~4 storeys (110k GSF / 2.2k m2) stepping down toward the park.

Former US Bureau of Mines main building, Hornbostel 1915-17 (Beaux-Arts, buff brick); CMU since 1985, Heinz College; renovated 2016. ~3 storeys + raised basement on Forbes, wings running back from Forbes; low hipped roofs of green Ludowici Spanish tile like the other Hornbostel buildings (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnegie_Mellon_University: "originally roofed with green Ludowici Spanish tile"), row of tall round-arched windows. height = eaves.

Wean Hall 1971 (Deeter Ritchey Sippel), Brutalist: tan concrete with deep spandrels and tinted, recessed glass bands (ikminc.com Wean Hall lobby project). 8 floors: ~4 below the Mall-level plaza (north side at ~29-32), ~4 above (~46); 293k GSF / 4.0k m2 ≈ 7 floors.
Gates & Hillman Centers 2009, Mack Scogin Merrill Elam; 9 storeys stepping down the ravine (lowest ~28). Zinc/aluminium panels + glass.
Newell-Simon Hall: Bureau of Mines lab building (1918/1934) renovated 1999. ~5 levels from the south yard (~22.6) = ~2 storeys above Forbes (169k GSF / 3.4k m2).

Highmark Center for Health, Wellness & Athletics (2024, Bohlin Cywinski Jackson): 4-storey, 154k sf, integrates Hornbostel's 1924 Skibo Gymnasium; buff brick + glass; terraced into the Schenley Park slope (50.6 → 64.7).

Alan Magee Scaife Hall of Engineering (2023, KieranTimberlake) replaced the 1962 Scaife Hall (OSM note: demolished 2020). 6 storeys terraced into the hillside; champagne aluminium panels/fins, glazed east face. Footprint is the old outline.
ANSYS Hall 2019 (Bohlin Cywinski Jackson), maker space / design studios, ~3 tall storeys, LEED Gold.
George A. Roberts Engineering Hall 1997 (72k GSF): on the edge of Junction Hollow beside Hamerschlag; roof ~ Hamerschlag Dr + 3 storeys.

Sherman & Joyce Bowie Scott Hall 2016 (OFFICE 52 / Stantec): 6-storey steel frame; North Wing cantilevers over Junction Hollow on angled white columns; dichroic-glass curtain wall; green roof/terrace links to Wean & Hamerschlag. Roof terrace ~y39 at the Wean/Hamerschlag plaza level. NOTE: build-data applies relation keys to every ring, so height is a deliberately small 8.5: placement.js clamps the main ring to ground.max+4 = 39.0 (21 m above the hollow) and gives the small pavilion ring 45.0 — both correct. See r13441031_0.

Soldiers and Sailors Memorial Hall (Henry Hornbostel 1907-10, Beaux-Arts, modelled on the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus): Rhode Island granite + Cleveland Gray sandstone with terra-cotta cornices, eight Doric columns over the entrance, cast-concrete stepped pyramidal roof reaching ~150 ft (pittsburghmuseums.org/.../soldiers-and-sailors-memorial-hall-and-museum; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soldiers_and_Sailors_Memorial_Hall_and_Museum). Generic approximation: eaves 30 m + pyramidal roof rise 14 m (builder max) → top ~44 m; levels 4 = podium + three storeys (sets the window rows). A dedicated landmark would model the podium, colonnades and stepped pyramid.

Pittsburgh Athletic Association clubhouse (Janssen & Abbott 1909-11): Venetian High Renaissance palazzo clad in limestone and terra cotta, stacked Corinthian orders, five storeys on a low podium, flat roof (theclio.com/entry/89907; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Athletic_Association). OSM roof:shape=quadruple_saltbox rendered a dark mansard — overridden.

Alumni Hall, former Masonic Temple (Benno Janssen 1914-15): classical temple clad mainly in limestone with a terra-cotta pediment and clay-tile roof; nine storeys with two-storey spaces; 200 ft along Fifth Avenue x 120 ft deep (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alumni_Hall_(University_of_Pittsburgh)). The real pediment faces Fifth (ridge across the short axis); the generic builder can only run a gable ridge along the long axis, so a low hipped clay-tile roof is used instead. height = eaves. OSM levels 4 kept on purpose: the builder draws one window row per level, and 4 tall rows read like the double-height tiers (9 rows looked like an office block).

Stephen Foster Memorial (Charles Klauder 1935-37): Gothic Revival companion to the Cathedral of Learning, steel frame faced with the same Indiana limestone (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Foster_Memorial); four-storey podium with bay windows, tall recessed Gothic arched entrance bays, buttresses and tracery (wje.com/projects/detail/stephen-foster-memorial) → OSM levels 4 kept, default gothic lancet facade. Colour = Cathedral stone (#cdc3ae in lm-oakland-a).

First Baptist Church, 159 N Bellefield (Bertram Goodhue, 1910-12, Gothic): cruciform stone church; a 182-ft filigreed copper spire rises from the crossing (sah-archipedia.org/buildings/PA-01-AL34, via search summary). The spire is not representable in curated data — flagged to lm-oakland-a. height = eaves; roof ridge ~26 m.

OSM building:levels=2 gave an 8 m box. Ground falls ~5.5 m across the footprint; height from the low side.
